mod3_membrane_structure.membranes_continuous_sheets_fusion: p33: membranes are continuous unbroken sheets enclosing compartments; structure allows fusion without losing continuity; plasma membrane separates cell from environment; internal membranes = nuclear envelope, mitochondrial, chloroplast, lysosomal, ER
mod3_membrane_structure.membrane_functions_seven: p33: compartmentalization; selectively permeable barrier; transporting solutes; scaffold for biochemical activities; responding to external signals (signal transduction); intercellular interaction; energy transduction
mod3_membrane_structure.membrane_components_lipid_protein_carb: p33-34: membranes made of lipids (mainly phospholipids), proteins, carbohydrates
mod3_membrane_structure.phospholipid_amphipathic_head_tail: p34: amphipathic; hydrophilic head = glycerol + phosphate + polar group; hydrophobic region = fatty acid tails
mod3_membrane_structure.micelle_vs_bilayer_head_size: p34: arrangement depends on head size; large bulky head + one tail -> micelle (sphere); smaller head + two tails -> bilayer with closed structure and inner space
mod3_membrane_structure.liposome_spontaneous_enclosure: p34: phospholipids in water spontaneously form enclosed bilayers = liposomes; enclose an inner space
mod3_membrane_structure.self_healing_membrane_hydrophobic_effect: p34: bilayer is self-healing, phospholipids spontaneously rearrange, due to tendency of water to exclude nonpolar molecules
mod3_membrane_structure.membrane_fluidity_lateral_movement: p35: membranes dynamic/fluid because lipids move laterally within the membrane
mod3_membrane_structure.fluidity_tail_length: p35: longer fatty acid tails = less fluid (decreased lipid mobility)
mod3_membrane_structure.fluidity_double_bonds: p35: fewer C=C double bonds = less fluid; saturated tails straight, pack tightly; unsaturated tails kinked, reduce packing, increase mobility
mod3_membrane_structure.cholesterol_fluidity_buffer: p35: cholesterol inserts into animal cell membranes; can increase or decrease fluidity depending on temperature (buffer); amphipathic OH head, rigid rings, hydrocarbon tail
mod3_membrane_structure.lipid_rafts_microdomains: p35: lipids and proteins in discrete regions = lipid rafts; specialized microdomains serving as platforms for cell processes
mod3_membrane_structure.lipid_flip_flop_rare_leaflet_asymmetry: p35: lipids move in plane of membrane; rarely flip-flop between layers; so the two layers can differ in composition
mod3_membrane_structure.integral_vs_peripheral_proteins: p36: integral = permanently associated, can span bilayer (transmembrane); peripheral = temporarily associated with bilayer or integral proteins via noncovalent bonds; cytoplasmic or extracellular
mod3_membrane_structure.transmembrane_protein: p36: integral protein spanning the entire bilayer
mod3_membrane_structure.membrane_carbohydrates_outward_glyco: p36: membrane carbohydrates all face extracellular space; covalently linked to protein (glycoprotein) or lipid (glycolipid)
mod3_membrane_structure.fluid_mosaic_model: p36: core is lipid bilayer; fluid (lateral movement); mosaic of lipids, proteins, carbohydrates; dynamic, transient interactions

mod3_endomembrane_system.internal_membranes_define_organelles: p37: eukaryotic cells have internal membranes defining organelles
mod3_endomembrane_system.animal_cell_organelle_roles: p37: ER synthesizes proteins & lipids; Golgi modifies, sorting station; lysosomes break down macromolecules; mitochondria harness energy; cytoskeleton protein scaffold; peroxisomes break down fatty acids, synthesize cholesterol/some phospholipids (Fig 3.9)
mod3_endomembrane_system.plant_cell_extras_wall_vacuole_chloropla: p37: plant cells also have cell wall (support), vacuoles (turgor pressure), chloroplasts (sunlight -> chemical energy)
mod3_endomembrane_system.cytoplasm_vs_cytosol: p37: cytoplasm = cell contents minus nucleus; cytosol = region outside organelles inside plasma membrane
mod3_endomembrane_system.ems_connected_bridges_or_vesicles: p37: internal membranes connected physically by membrane bridges or transiently by vesicles that bud off an organelle
mod3_endomembrane_system.ems_definition_components: p38: endomembrane system = interconnected organelles: plasma membrane, nuclear envelope, ER, Golgi, lysosomes, vesicles; allows functions in defined spaces
mod3_endomembrane_system.nucleus_innermost_ems: p38: nucleus is innermost organelle of the EMS
mod3_endomembrane_system.nuclear_envelope_double_membrane: p38: nuclear envelope is a double membrane (inner and outer)
mod3_endomembrane_system.nuclear_pores_passive_small_active_large: p38: nuclear pores let molecules move in/out; small molecules and ions diffuse passively, large proteins and RNA need active transport; essential for communication
mod3_endomembrane_system.er_continuous_outer_nuclear_membrane: p38: outer nuclear membrane is physically continuous with the ER
mod3_endomembrane_system.er_tubules_sacs_surface_area: p38: ER network of tubules and flattened sacs; highly folded -> large surface area; produces many lipids and proteins
mod3_endomembrane_system.rough_er_ribosomes_protein_synthesis: p39: RER has ribosomes (exposed to cytosol); ribosomes = protein synthesis sites; ribosomes also free in cytosol
mod3_endomembrane_system.smooth_er_lipid_synthesis_vesicles: p39: SER lacks ribosomes; buds vesicles; site of fatty acid and phospholipid synthesis; abundant in lipid-producing cells
mod3_endomembrane_system.golgi_not_attached_next_stop: p39: Golgi not physically attached to ER; next stop for vesicles budding from ER
mod3_endomembrane_system.golgi_three_functions: p39: Golgi further modifies proteins/lipids, sorts them to destinations, adds carbohydrates
mod3_endomembrane_system.golgi_cisternae_regional_enzymes: p39: Golgi = flattened sacs (cisternae) with vesicles; each modification step in a different region with different enzymes
mod3_endomembrane_system.glycosylation: p39: glycosylation = carbohydrates (glycans) covalently linked to lipids or specific amino acids of proteins
mod3_endomembrane_system.lysosome_golgi_derived_degradation: p40: lysosomes are specialized vesicles derived from Golgi; degrade damaged/unneeded proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, complex carbohydrates
mod3_endomembrane_system.lysosomal_enzymes_rer_golgi_path: p40: lysosomal enzymes synthesized in RER -> sorted in Golgi -> packaged into lysosomes
mod3_endomembrane_system.lysosome_proton_pump_ph5: p40: lysosome membrane proton pump keeps internal pH ~5
mod3_endomembrane_system.lysosome_separation_protects_cytosol: p40: contents kept separate because cytosol is ~pH 7; cytosolic proteins/organelles would degrade at pH 5

mod3_mito_chloro.mito_chloro_not_ems: p41: mitochondria and chloroplasts are membranous but not part of the EMS
mod3_mito_chloro.semi_autonomous_circular_genomes: p41: semi-autonomous: grow and multiply independently, contain own circular genomes; both harness energy
mod3_mito_chloro.mitochondria_chemical_energy_to_atp: p41: mitochondria harness energy from compounds like sugars into ATP; rod-shaped; in almost all eukaryotic cells
mod3_mito_chloro.mito_outer_membrane_porins: p41: outer membrane integral proteins form large nonselective channels = porins
mod3_mito_chloro.mito_intermembrane_space: p41: aqueous compartment between outer and inner membranes
mod3_mito_chloro.mito_inner_membrane_etc_atp_synthase: p41: inner membrane highly convoluted; electron transport chain and ATP synthase
mod3_mito_chloro.mito_matrix_cac_ribosomes_dna: p41: matrix contains citric acid cycle, ribosomes, DNA
mod3_mito_chloro.chloroplast_photosynthesis_sugars: p41: chloroplasts capture sun's energy to synthesize simple sugars
mod3_mito_chloro.chloroplast_double_membrane_plus_thylako: p41-42: double membrane plus internal membrane-bound compartment (thylakoid) = third membrane
mod3_mito_chloro.thylakoid_pigments_chlorophyll: p42: thylakoid membrane contains light-collecting pigments; chlorophyll most common (green)
mod3_mito_chloro.chloroplast_lumen_grana_stroma: p42: thylakoids = flattened sacs; lumen = space inside a thylakoid; grana = stacks; stroma = space surrounding thylakoids
mod3_mito_chloro.endosymbiosis_chloroplast_cyanobacteria: p42: chloroplasts resemble cyanobacteria; originated from cyanobacterium engulfed by a eukaryotic cell
mod3_mito_chloro.endosymbiosis_mitochondria_proteobacteri: p42: mitochondria resemble free-living bacteria; originated as endosymbiotic proteobacteria
mod3_mito_chloro.eukaryote_origin_two_hypotheses: p42 Fig 3.18: H1 archaeon evolves nucleus/EMS first (membrane infolding) then engulfs proteobacterium; H2 archaeon-proteobacterium symbiosis first, infolding later

mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.selective_permeability_size_polarity: p43: gases (O2, CO2) and nonpolar molecules cross; small uncharged polar (H2O) cross; macromolecules (proteins, carbohydrates) too large
mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.influx_efflux_net_flux: p43: movement in = influx, out = efflux; when one exceeds the other = net flux
mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.diffusion_net_movement_equilibrium: p43: diffusion spontaneous; net movement high->low; net movement stops at no gradient but random motion continues both ways
mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.passive_transport_down_gradient: p43: passive transport via diffusion, driven by concentration gradient (no energy input)
mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.simple_diffusion_small_hydrophobic: p43: simple diffusion directly through membrane: small molecules (O2, CO2), hydrophobic molecules (e.g. triacylglycerols)
mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.facilitated_diffusion_protein: p44: facilitated diffusion = down gradient through a protein transporter
mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.channel_proteins_pore_selective_gated: p44: channels formed by integral proteins surrounding an aqueous pore; selective; some gated (open/closed)
mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.carrier_proteins_conformational_change: p44: carriers bind specific molecule, conformational change exposes it to other side, diffuses down gradient
mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.osmosis_water_diffusion: p45: osmosis = diffusion of water across semipermeable membrane from higher [H2O] to lower [H2O]
mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.osmotic_pressure_tonicity: p45: osmotic pressure; tonicity of surrounding solution matters
mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.isotonic: p45: equal solute on both sides = isotonic
mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.hypertonic_crenation_plasmolysis: p45: hypertonic (higher solute outside) -> water leaves, cell shrinks; animal cells shrivel (crenation); plant cells pull away from wall (plasmolysis)
mod3_passive_transport_osmosis.hypotonic_lysis_turgor: p45: hypotonic (lower solute outside) -> water enters, cell swells; animal cells burst (RBC hemolysis/lysis); plant cells push against wall (turgor)

mod3_active_transport.active_transport_against_gradient_energy: p46: movement against concentration gradient needs energy; protein carrier (active transporter)
mod3_active_transport.active_transporter_one_direction: p46: transporter changes conformation upon binding -> movement in one direction
mod3_active_transport.primary_vs_secondary_active: p46-47: primary uses chemical energy of ATP directly; secondary uses an electrochemical gradient
mod3_active_transport.na_k_pump_3na_2k_atp: p46: Na+/K+-ATPase, only in animal cells; ATP hydrolysis moves 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in against gradients; ions move in opposite directions (antiport)
mod3_active_transport.na_k_pump_cycle_steps: p46: Na+ binds inside -> ATP hydrolyzed (pump phosphorylated) -> conformation change -> Na+ released outside -> K+ binds outside -> phosphate removed -> pump snaps back -> K+ released inside
mod3_active_transport.electrochemical_gradient: p47: gradient with electrical (charge) and chemical component; established by primary active transport; inside negative/outside positive; drives secondary transport
mod3_active_transport.proton_pump_gradient: p47: cells can pump protons with ATP, creating a proton concentration (chemical) gradient that is also electrical because protons are charged
mod3_active_transport.secondary_active_cotransport: p47: movement of an ion down its gradient drives another molecule against its gradient = secondary active transport (co-transport)
mod3_active_transport.antiport_symport_uniport: p48: antiport = opposite directions (e.g. Na+ and H+); symport = same direction (e.g. Na+ and glucose); uniporter moves one solute
mod3_active_transport.intestinal_glucose_transport: p48: apical membrane Na+ entry drives glucose co-transport into intestinal cell against its gradient; glucose diffuses through cytoplasm; basal membrane facilitated diffusion into blood; Na+/K+ pump keeps inside Na+ low

mod3_bulk_transport.bulk_transport_membrane_continuity: p49: bulk transport moves large molecules/particles without breaking membrane continuity
mod3_bulk_transport.exocytosis: p49: vesicle from EMS fuses with plasma membrane, delivers contents to extracellular space
mod3_bulk_transport.endocytosis_invagination: p49: membrane invaginates forming pocket, pinches off into a new intracellular vesicle from the plasma membrane
mod3_bulk_transport.phagocytosis_phagosome_lysosome: p49: phagocytosis: particle in phagosome; fuses with primary lysosome -> secondary lysosome activates hydrolytic enzymes; digestion; recognition via receptor
mod3_bulk_transport.phagocytosis_nutrition_defense: p50: nutrition; defense by macrophages and neutrophils; lysozyme degrades bacterial cell walls; acidic pH kills; oxidases make H2O2
mod3_bulk_transport.pinocytosis_nonspecific: p50: 'cell drinking'; fluid taken up without recognition; smaller vesicles; need not merge with lysosome; any dissolved molecules enter
mod3_bulk_transport.receptor_mediated_endocytosis: p50: receptors with binding specificity concentrated at coated pits; clathrin on cytoplasmic side; brings specific cargo in
mod3_bulk_transport.early_late_endosomes: p50: material delivered to endosomes; early endosomes near periphery; late endosomes interior, receive from early endosomes and Golgi

mod4_dna_evidence_structure.dna_store_and_copy: p53: DNA structure common to all organisms; linked to function: storing genetic info and copying itself to transmit it
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.chromosome_condensation_histones: p53 Fig 4.1: 2 nm DNA -> 10 nm nucleosome fiber (histones H2A, H2B, H3, H4) -> 30 nm chromatin fiber -> 300 nm -> 700 nm -> 1400 nm condensed chromatid
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.griffith_1928_transformation: p53-54: S. pneumoniae virulent vs nonvirulent; heat-killed virulent + live nonvirulent -> mouse dies; a molecule in the debris carried virulence info; not identified then
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.avery_1944_enzyme_logic: p54: extract + RNase or protease still transforms; + DNase does not -> DNA is the transforming (genetic) material
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.nucleotide_three_parts_carbons: p55: nucleotide = deoxyribose (no O at 2'), base at 1' carbon, phosphate(s) (on 5' carbon)
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.nucleotide_vs_nucleoside: p55: nucleotide three parts; nucleoside just base + sugar
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.purines_ag_pyrimidines_ct: p55: purines A, G (double ring); pyrimidines T, C (single ring)
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.backbone_sugar_phosphate_negative: p55: sugar + phosphate form backbone; two negative charges on phosphate from hydroxyl ionization at pH ~7
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.strand_polarity_5p_3p: p55: strand has free 5' phosphate end and free 3' hydroxyl end
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.sequence_convention_left_5prime: p55: 5'-AGCT-3' = 3'-TCGA-5'; unlabeled sequence: left end is 5'
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.dna_grows_5_to_3: p55: bases only added to 3'-OH; DNA grows 5' to 3'
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.watson_crick_franklin_chargaff: p56: Watson & Crick model built on Franklin & Wilkins X-ray data and Chargaff's %C=%G, %A=%T
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.double_helix_right_handed_outside_inside: p56: two strands form right-handed helix; sugar-phosphate backbones outside; bases inward
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.antiparallel_strands: p56: two strands run in opposite directions (antiparallel)
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.major_minor_grooves: p56: outside contours form uneven major and minor grooves
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.complementary_base_pairs: p56: A pairs only with T, C only with G = complementary base pairs
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.hbonds_gc3_at2: p57: 3 H-bonds between G and C; 2 between A and T; H-bonds give pairing specificity
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.dna_stability_hbonds_stacking: p57: stability from many weak H-bonds plus base stacking (interactions between bases on the same strand)
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.weak_hbonds_allow_unzipping: p57: weak H-bonds let DNA unzip down the middle
mod4_dna_evidence_structure.helix_dimensions: p56 Fig 4.8: 3.4 nm (10 base pairs) per turn; 2 nm diameter

mod4_gene_expression_rna.genome_definition: p58: genome = genetic material of an organism: bacterial, nuclear, mitochondrial genomes
mod4_gene_expression_rna.gene_definition: p58: gene = unit of heredity affecting traits; DNA sequence corresponding to a specific protein
mod4_gene_expression_rna.gene_expression_regulated: p58: gene expression = production of a functional gene product such as a protein; regulated; genes on/off
mod4_gene_expression_rna.central_dogma_flow: p58: DNA transcribed into RNA, translated into protein
mod4_gene_expression_rna.transcription_same_language: p58: transcription = RNA from DNA template; same nucleic acid language
mod4_gene_expression_rna.translation_language_change: p58: translation = change of language from nucleic acids to amino acids; depends on mRNA code
mod4_gene_expression_rna.reverse_transcription_hiv: p58: exception: reverse transcriptase (RNA-dependent DNA polymerase) makes DNA from RNA, e.g. HIV
mod4_gene_expression_rna.transcription_location_prok_euk: p59: prokaryotes transcription and translation in cytoplasm; eukaryotes transcription in nucleus, translation in cytoplasm
mod4_gene_expression_rna.rna_polarity: p60: RNA also has 5' phosphate and 3' hydroxyl polarity
mod4_gene_expression_rna.rna_ribose_2oh_less_stable: p60: ribose has OH at 2' carbon; makes RNA less stable than DNA
mod4_gene_expression_rna.uracil_replaces_thymine: p60: uracil replaces thymine (U has H where T has CH3); A pairs with U in RNA
mod4_gene_expression_rna.rna_5prime_triphosphate: p60: RNA 5' end typically triphosphate; DNA 5' end monophosphate
mod4_gene_expression_rna.rna_shorter_single_folds: p60: RNA usually shorter, mostly single stranded, folds into complex shapes

mod4_transcription_mechanism.transcription_complementary_copy: p61: transcription creates complementary RNA copy of a DNA sequence; similar in prokaryotes and eukaryotes
mod4_transcription_mechanism.transcription_requirements: p61: needs DNA template, RNA polymerase, ribonucleotide triphosphates (building blocks + energy for synthesis)
mod4_transcription_mechanism.template_vs_nontemplate: p61: one strand is template; RNA matches the nontemplate strand except U for T
mod4_transcription_mechanism.pol_reads_3to5_rna_5to3: p61: RNA polymerase moves 3'->5' along template; RNA grows 5'->3'
mod4_transcription_mechanism.all_nucleic_acids_add_to_3prime: p61: all nucleic acids synthesized by adding nucleotides to the 3' end
mod4_transcription_mechanism.promoter_conserved_binding_site: p62: initiation at promoter: conserved double-stranded sequence bound by transcription factors and RNA polymerase
mod4_transcription_mechanism.tata_box_25bp: p62: common eukaryotic promoter element 5'-TATAAA-3' (TATA box); first transcribed nucleotide ~25 bp away
mod4_transcription_mechanism.terminator: p62: transcription proceeds until RNA polymerase reaches a terminator
mod4_transcription_mechanism.template_strand_varies_by_gene: p62 Fig 4.14: which strand is transcribed can differ from one gene to the next
mod4_transcription_mechanism.bacterial_sigma_factor: p62: bacterial promoter recognition by sigma factor associating with RNA Pol; single type of RNA Pol in prokaryotes
mod4_transcription_mechanism.eukaryotic_general_tfs_pol_ii: p62: at least six general transcription factors bind promoter; 3 distinct RNA polymerases; RNA Pol II makes mRNA
mod4_transcription_mechanism.enhancers_activators_mediator_looping: p62-63: activators bind enhancers; mediator complex links GTFs and Pol II; DNA looping brings activators to promoter proteins
mod4_transcription_mechanism.transcription_bubble: p63: bubble ~14 bp; RNA-DNA duplex in bubble ~8 bp
mod4_transcription_mechanism.elongation_channels: p63: polymerase unwinds DNA; channels for NTP entry, DNA entry/exit, RNA exit
mod4_transcription_mechanism.polymerization_chemistry: p64: incoming NTP accepted if it base-pairs; 3'-OH of growing strand attacks innermost phosphate of NTP (energy); pyrophosphate released; permanent attachment

mod4_prok_euk_processing.primary_transcript: p65: RNA transcript coming off template = primary transcript
mod4_prok_euk_processing.prok_primary_transcript_is_mrna: p65: in prokaryotes the primary transcript is the mRNA (simpler)
mod4_prok_euk_processing.coupled_transcription_translation: p65: no nuclear envelope; transcription and translation coupled; translation begins before transcription is complete
mod4_prok_euk_processing.polycistronic_mrna: p65: prokaryotic primary transcript may contain info for more than one gene = polycistronic mRNA
mod4_prok_euk_processing.eukaryotic_processing_why: p65: nuclear membrane adds complexity; primary transcript must be modified (RNA processing) to move from nucleus to cytoplasm
mod4_prok_euk_processing.five_prime_cap: p66: 7-methylguanosine cap added to 5' end via unique 5'-5' (triphosphate) bond; protects from exonucleases, stability; needed for ribosome recognition/translation
mod4_prok_euk_processing.poly_a_tail: p66: ~250 adenines added to 3' end (polyadenylation); roles in termination, export to cytoplasm, protection from exonucleases
mod4_prok_euk_processing.introns_exons_splicing: p66: introns excised, exons joined = RNA splicing
mod4_prok_euk_processing.alternative_splicing: p66: one gene's primary transcript spliced different ways -> different related proteins in different cells (e.g. E1-E2-E4 vs E1-E2-E3)

bridge_links_m12.m1_ems_classification: M1: EMS = membrane trafficking participation; vacuole, nuclear envelope, plasma membrane, lysosomes EMS; mitochondria, chloroplast, peroxisome, ribosome, nucleolus, cytoskeleton non-EMS
bridge_links_m12.m1_prokaryote_no_nucleus: M1: prokaryotes lack nucleus and membrane-bound organelles
bridge_links_m12.m1_three_domain_eukarya_from_archaea: M1: Eukarya branches from within Archaea
bridge_links_m12.m1_cell_properties: M1: 8 basic properties (membrane-enclosed; genetic program; reproduction; energy; metabolism; mechanical; responds to stimuli; self-regulation)
bridge_links_m12.m1_plant_wall_vacuole_turgor: M1: plant cellulose wall + central vacuole turgor; animal cells lack wall
bridge_links_m12.m1_model_organisms: M1: E. coli for DNA replication/transcription/translation etc.
bridge_links_m12.m1_virus_exception: M1: viruses are exceptions to cell theory
bridge_links_m12.m1_nucleolus_rrna_ribosome: M1: nucleolus non-membrane region making rRNA/assembling ribosomes
bridge_links_m12.m2_phospholipid_amphipathic: M2: phospholipid = glycerol + 2 tails + phosphate head, amphipathic; triacylglycerol 3 tails hydrophobic
bridge_links_m12.m2_saturated_unsaturated: M2: double bonds kink tails, looser packing
bridge_links_m12.m2_cholesterol_steroid: M2: cholesterol = steroid, four fused rings
bridge_links_m12.m2_water_polarity_hbonds_hydration: M2: water polar, H-bonds, hydration shells, hydrophobic effect
bridge_links_m12.m2_ph_log_scale: M2: pH log scale, each unit 10x [H+]
bridge_links_m12.m2_phosphodiester_5to3: M2: phosphodiester bond links phosphate to next 3'-OH; 5'->3'
bridge_links_m12.m2_purine_pyrimidine_ribose: M2: purines A,G; pyrimidines C,T,U; ribose 2'-OH more reactive
bridge_links_m12.m2_condensation_hydrolysis_energy: M2: condensation releases water and needs energy; hydrolysis releases energy
bridge_links_m12.m2_atp_phosphate_bonds: M2: ATP high-energy bonds between phosphates
bridge_links_m12.m2_protein_functions_structure: M2: protein functions (enzyme, transport, signal, support...), R-groups, folding
bridge_links_m12.m2_functional_groups_charge: M2: phosphate negatively charged; amino/carboxyl ionizable
bridge_links_m12.m2_hydrogen_bond_definition: M2: hydrogen bond definition, weak individually
